scope: The money trail into and around India's energy and natural-resources sector: ECI-published electoral-bond purchases matched to parties (12 Apr 2019–24 Jan 2024) for energy, power, mining, oil-gas and hydro/EPC purchasers; declared direct donations and electoral-trust routing for FY2023-24 and FY2024-25 (ADR analyses of ECI filings); PM CARES contributions by energy PSUs and private groups; PSU CSR concentration where a primary record could be opened; base rates and a symmetry check on opposition-run states. It records the documented absence of Adani, Reliance and Tata from the bond purchaser list alongside their other channels. Deliberately left out: contract awards and clearances themselves (coal.json, mines.json, solarwind.json, nuclear.json), enforcement histories beyond one cross-reference (enforce.json), non-energy purchasers except where needed for base rates or symmetry (Future Gaming, Qwik, Kolkata trio, Tata), and any figure whose only source is the blocked ECI portal.

entities.sub: Corporate political-donation clause; 7.5%-of-average-net-profit cap deleted by Finance Act 2017
d: The Finance Act 2017 deleted the cap limiting corporate political donations to 7.5% of average net profits of the three preceding years; the Supreme Court on 2024-02-15 held the deletion violative of Article 14 [documented]

narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: A donor-level regression of party share on incumbency at the level that awards the donor's contracts; a control period (2014–17 cheque donations) showing a different incumbency premium.

symmetryCheck: Control set: opposition-run states and their incumbents, using the same lens. (1) West Bengal: Haldia Energy (RPSG, whose CESC holds the Kolkata distribution licence regulated by WBERC) gave AITC ₹281 cr and BJP ₹81 cr — a 3.5:1 incumbent premium, larger than MEIL's 3:1 for BJP over BRS. (2) Odisha: the three largest BJD donors are the state's mining lessees and metals plants — Essel Mining ₹174.5 cr, JSPL ₹100 cr, Utkal Alumina ₹70 cr — exactly the resource-rent pattern the BJP-side narrative alleges. (3) Telangana: MEIL gave the BRS ₹195 cr while the BRS government was its Kaleshwaram client, and The Hindu documented IRB Infra's ₹25 cr bonds bought 68 days after a BRS LoA and encashed nine days later; Prudent also gave BRS ₹85 cr in FY24. (4) Tamil Nadu/AP: Future Gaming (ED-probed) gave DMK ₹503–509 cr and YSRCP ₹154 cr; MEIL gave DMK ₹85–105 cr and YSRCP ₹37 cr; Shirdi Sai gave TDP ₹40 cr while TDP was in opposition. (5) Karnataka: JD(S) disclosed ₹50 cr from Megha Engineering and ₹22 cr from Embassy (sole bidder for a Bengaluru pod-taxi project weeks before donating). Result: the identical method produces an equally alarming graph for every incumbent at the level that awards contracts and leases; what differs is scale (the Centre awards most) and the post-2024 concentration (82.5% of trust money to BJP versus ~47.5% of bonds). The lens therefore detects incumbency rent-seeking generally; it does not, by itself, distinguish quid pro quo from goodwill, and no claim in this file should be read as doing so.
